label: Kite & wind
blurb: Kitesurf and windsurf spots with reliable wind and room to launch.

places.name: Playa de los Lances, Tarifa
places.why: Europe's kite capital: Levante or Poniente blows most days over a 7 km beach, with dozens of schools on the sand.

places.name: Valdevaqueros, Tarifa
places.why: The Levante funnel spot with a dune backdrop; strong, gusty offshore-ish wind, so most riders are experienced.

places.name: Pozo Izquierdo
places.why: PWA wave venue with brutal summer trade winds and a rocky shore; the world's top windsurfers jump here every July.

places.name: Playa de Vargas
places.why: Pozo's slightly friendlier neighbour, still side-onshore trades of 25–40 knots over a pebble beach.

places.name: Sotavento, Fuerteventura
places.why: Tidal lagoon behind a sandbar; flat inside, chop outside, and the PWA Fuerteventura slalom and freestyle since 1986.

places.name: Flag Beach, Corralejo
places.why: Long sandy beach in the Corralejo dunes; steady side-shore trades and Lobos island for shelter.

places.name: El Médano
places.why: Windy town beach under Montaña Roja, PWA wave venue with side-shore trades and a mellow bay for learners.

places.name: Famara, Lanzarote
places.why: 5 km wave beach under the Risco cliffs; onshore trades and reliable swell for wave kiting.

places.name: Sant Pere Pescador
places.why: The Tramuntana blows offshore-ish and hard across the Gulf of Roses; long beach with schools at the river mouth.

places.name: Oliva
places.why: Kite-designated beach zone with thermal sea breeze most summer afternoons.

places.name: Praia do Guincho
places.why: The Nortada blows side-shore over Atlantic swell all summer; PWA wave venue and a serious rip for beginners.

places.name: Lagoa de Óbidos
places.why: Big shallow lagoon with Nortada afternoons; standing-depth flat water for lessons and freestyle.

places.name: Alvor
places.why: Estuary lagoon at low tide gives flat shallow water; gentle thermals suit learners.

places.name: Baleal
places.why: Sheltered north bay next to Peniche's surf breaks; Nortada wind and small waves.

places.name: Cabedelo, Viana do Castelo
places.why: PWA slalom and wave venue at the Lima river mouth; strong summer Nortada.

places.name: La Franqui, Leucate
places.why: Home of the Mondial du Vent; the Tramontane delivers 30-knot days over a long beach and shallow shorebreak.

places.name: Gruissan
places.why: Tramontane-swept lagoon and beach in the Défi Wind area; huge kite and windsurf scene.

places.name: L'Almanarre, Hyères
places.why: Mistral hits this long spit side-shore; flat on the Giens side, chop on the sea side.

places.name: Plage de Beauduc
places.why: Remote Camargue spit reached by dirt track; Mistral flat water and few crowds.

places.name: Wissant
places.why: Wide sand bay between the two caps; south-westerlies and Channel swell for wave riding.

places.name: Penthièvre, Quiberon
places.why: Isthmus beach that works on either wind side; shallow and sandy for lessons.

places.name: Lo Stagnone, Marsala
places.why: Knee-deep lagoon with a thermal breeze most afternoons; one of Europe's busiest learning spots.

places.name: Porto Pollo
places.why: Isthmus between two bays; Mistral and Ponente give flat water on one side and chop on the other.

places.name: Punta Trettu
places.why: Shallow lagoon in the south-west corner of Sardinia; Mistral and Scirocco both work.

places.name: Torbole, Lake Garda
places.why: The Ora thermal blows every summer afternoon; a windsurf classic with mountain scenery.

places.name: Lake Silvaplana
places.why: The Maloja wind arrives at noon like clockwork over a 1,800 m alpine lake; foil and freestyle heaven.

places.name: Isleten, Lake Uri
places.why: Foehn funnel on Lake Lucerne's southern arm; strong, warm gusts when the pressure gradient is right.

places.name: Podersdorf, Neusiedler See
places.why: Waist-deep steppe lake with reliable wind; surf world cup venue and a big freestyle scene.

places.name: Brouwersdam
places.why: The Netherlands' flagship spot on the dam between sea and lake; flat inside, waves outside.

places.name: Wijk aan Zee
places.why: Beach north of the IJmuiden pier that takes the wave end of Dutch kiting; SW winds and chop.

places.name: Westerland, Sylt
places.why: The Windsurf World Cup finale since 1984; autumn North Sea storms and a raw, cold shorebreak.

places.name: St. Peter-Ording
places.why: Kilometre-wide flat beach and standing-depth water at low tide; Kitesurf World Cup venue.

places.name: Gold, Fehmarn
places.why: Baltic spot that works in westerlies with shallow flat water; Fehmarn hosts the Kitesurf Trophy.

places.name: Klitmøller
places.why: 'Cold Hawaii': a fishing village with PWA wave contests and a reef point for North Sea wave sailing.

places.name: Lakolk, Rømø
places.why: You can drive onto a beach hundreds of metres wide; shallow water and steady westerlies.

places.name: Hvide Sande
places.why: Harbour moles and a long beach on Denmark's windiest coast; wave sailing and kiting.

places.name: Chałupy, Hel Peninsula
places.why: Puck Bay's shallow lagoon side is Poland's kite nursery, with dozens of schools along the spit.

places.name: Apelviken, Varberg
places.why: Sweden's best-known surf and kite bay; west winds bring swell into the sandy cove.

places.name: Yyteri
places.why: Long dune beach on the Bothnian Sea; Finland's main windsurf and kite spot in summer westerlies.

places.name: Hayling Island
places.why: Birthplace of windsurfing's British scene; Chichester Harbour entrance gives flat water at low tide.

places.name: Camber Sands
places.why: Vast low-tide beach with Channel breezes; the UK's busiest kite beach close to London.

places.name: Rhosneigr
places.why: Twin bays with a mix of flat water and Irish Sea waves; a dedicated kite and windsurf village.

places.name: Gott Bay, Tiree
places.why: The Tiree Wave Classic has run here since 1986; Atlantic swell and gales on a treeless island.

places.name: Poole Harbour
places.why: Shallow, sheltered harbour with flat water and easy tides; the south coast's learner spot.

places.name: Hunstanton
places.why: West-facing Wash beach with cross-shore SW winds and huge tidal flats; wave and flat mix.

places.name: Marazion
places.why: Mount's Bay beach in front of St Michael's Mount; works in the SW wind Cornwall gets most.

places.name: Dollymount Strand
places.why: Bull Island's long beach inside Dublin Bay; shallow flat water at low tide minutes from the city.

places.name: Prasonisi
places.why: Sandbar at Rhodes' southern tip: Meltemi gives flat water on one side and waves on the other.

places.name: Ixia
places.why: Rhodes' windsurf strip near the city; Meltemi side-shore over a pebble beach.

places.name: Vasiliki
places.why: 'Eric' the thermal wind arrives every afternoon across the bay; a windsurf mecca since the 1980s.

places.name: New Golden Beach, Paros
places.why: Meltemi funnels across the strait to Naxos; PWA slalom venue in the 1990s.

places.name: Pounda, Paros
places.why: Kite beach facing Antiparos; Meltemi side-shore and a shallow strait.

places.name: Mikri Vigla, Naxos
places.why: Twin bays under a headland: flat lagoon for kiting and small waves; strongest Meltemi in the Cyclades.

places.name: Marmari, Kos
places.why: Long north-coast beach with a stable Meltemi; a good learning spot with several schools.

places.name: Afiartis (Devil's Bay)
places.why: Some of Europe's strongest Meltemi, 30–40 knots side-shore across a shallow bay near the airport.

places.name: Keros Beach, Lemnos
places.why: Shallow sandy bay in the north Aegean with steady Meltemi and dune-backed beach.

places.name: Kouremenos
places.why: Crete's east-coast windsurf and kite bay; strong summer Meltemi accelerates between the hills.

places.name: Zlatni Rat, Bol
places.why: The Maestral blows each summer afternoon across the famous golden spit.

places.name: Viganj
places.why: Channel between Pelješac and Korčula where the Maestral accelerates; Croatia's windsurf village.

places.name: Alaçatı Windsurf Bay
places.why: Shallow bay sheltered from waves with steady Meltemi; PWA slalom venue and a wall of schools.

places.name: Aydıncık, Gökçeada
places.why: Island bay with salt lake behind; Meltemi side-shore and hardly any crowds.

places.name: Akyaka
places.why: Head of the Gulf of Gökova where a thermal funnels through the valley; flat water for kites.

places.name: Eilat
places.why: Northerly desert wind on the Gulf of Aqaba almost year-round; beach zones for kite and windsurf.

places.name: Dakhla Lagoon
places.why: 28 km lagoon with 300 windy days a year; camps line the shore and the GKA tour stops here.

places.name: Essaouira
places.why: Crescent bay where the trade wind is strongest in summer; kiting off the medina beach.

places.name: Moulay Bouzerktoun
places.why: Rocky wave spot north of Essaouira; strong side-offshore trades and Atlantic swell.

places.name: Sidi Kaouki
places.why: Wide, empty beach 25 km south of Essaouira; cleaner waves and less wind than the town.

places.name: Djerba Ras R'mel
places.why: Flat lagoon behind a sand spit at Djerba's north tip; easy learning water in the Mediterranean.

places.name: El Gouna Mangroovy
places.why: Shallow lagoon in front of the kite centres; winter and summer both windy, and the GKA has raced here.

places.name: Soma Bay
places.why: Peninsula resort with a huge shallow flat and reliable northerlies.

places.name: Safaga
places.why: Kite and windsurf bay with Tobia island's sandbank flats a short boat ride away.

places.name: Ras Sudr
places.why: Gulf of Suez desert coast two hours from Cairo; wind almost every day and thigh-deep flat water.

places.name: Dahab Lagoon
places.why: Mountain-backed lagoon with a thermal that fills in daily; sheltered flat water for learners.

places.name: Hamata
places.why: Remote southern Red Sea kite camp; shallow reef lagoon and few other riders.

places.name: Kite Beach, Sal
places.why: Trade winds from November to May across a wide east-coast bay; Cape Verde's kite hub.

places.name: Ponta Preta, Sal
places.why: Long right-hand point wave off Sal's south-west tip; a PWA and GKA wave-contest venue.

places.name: Praia de Chaves, Boa Vista
places.why: Miles of dune-backed beach on Boa Vista's west coast with trade wind and small waves.

places.name: Almadies, Dakar
places.why: Africa's westernmost point picks up Harmattan trade winds and Atlantic swell in winter.

places.name: Diani Beach
places.why: Reef-protected lagoon at low tide with Kaskazi and Kusi monsoon winds; Kenya's kite centre.

places.name: Watamu
places.why: Marine park lagoon with monsoon winds; flat inside the reef, small waves at the passes.

places.name: Paje
places.why: Turquoise lagoon so shallow you can stand for a kilometre; the Kusi and Kaskazi seasons both blow.

places.name: Jambiani
places.why: Quieter village south of Paje on the same reef lagoon; same winds, fewer kites.

places.name: Vilanculos
places.why: Bazaruto archipelago waters with a shallow flat and side-onshore southerlies.

places.name: Praia do Tofo
places.why: Open-ocean bay with south-easterlies and swell; kite next to whale-shark diving.

places.name: Sakalava Bay
places.why: Reef-sheltered bay near Madagascar's north tip; the Varatraza trade blows 25 knots for eight months.

places.name: Le Morne
places.why: Kite lagoon under the UNESCO mountain, with One Eye's wave outside; the GKA has run waves here.

places.name: Anse La Raie
places.why: North-coast lagoon with easterly trades; flat, shallow and quieter than Le Morne.

places.name: Saint-Pierre
places.why: Réunion's kite beach on the south-west coast with steady trades and reef swell.

places.name: Langebaan Lagoon
places.why: Shark Bay's shallow flat water in the West Coast National Park; summer southerly blows daily.

places.name: Kite Beach, Blouberg
places.why: Table Mountain in the frame and the Cape Doctor blowing 25–35 knots; the Red Bull King of the Air venue.

places.name: Big Bay
places.why: Bloubergstrand's northern bay: same summer south-easter, slightly more sheltered than Kite Beach.

places.name: Witsand
places.why: Breede river mouth with a long flat sandbar; strong summer south-easters and few crowds.

places.name: Walvis Bay Lagoon
places.why: Desert lagoon with flamingos and a stiff south-westerly; Namibia's kite and speed sailing base.

places.name: Lüderitz Speed Channel
places.why: Purpose-dug 500 m trench where outright windsurf and kite speed records were set.

places.name: Masirah Island
places.why: Khareef monsoon lagoon on Masirah's west coast; 20–30 knots daily in the northern summer.

places.name: Kite Beach, Jumeirah
places.why: City beach with a kite-only zone and the Burj Al Arab skyline; winter and spring sea breezes.

places.name: Kalpitiya Lagoon
places.why: Butter-flat lagoon between peninsula and sea; two monsoon seasons make it Asia's freestyle school.

places.name: Kappalady Lagoon
places.why: Smaller lagoon south of Kalpitiya, shallower and less crowded, same monsoon winds.

places.name: Rameswaram
places.why: Shallow bay on India's south-east tip with south-west monsoon wind; the only major Indian kite spot.

places.name: Mui Ne
places.why: Vietnam's kite strip: north-east monsoon wind from November to April and chop for jumping.

places.name: Hua Hin
places.why: Kiteboard World Cup venue with two seasons of onshore thermals; shallow and beginner-friendly.

places.name: Pak Nam Pran
places.why: Quieter beach south of Hua Hin with the same seasonal winds and less traffic.

places.name: Sanur
places.why: Reef lagoon on Bali's east coast with dry-season trades; flat inside, waves at the reef.

places.name: Bulabog Beach
places.why: Reef-protected flat water with the Amihan trade wind from November to April; dozens of schools.

places.name: Bagasbas Beach, Daet
places.why: Long grey-sand beach on the Pacific coast that hosts national kite contests in the Amihan season.

places.name: Penghu
places.why: Taiwan Strait monsoon blows 25 knots for months; Penghu is Taiwan's windsurf training base.

places.name: Pingtan
places.why: Taiwan Strait wind funnel that hosts the PWA slalom and RS:X events.

places.name: Shinyang Beach, Jeju
places.why: Jeju's windsurf beach on the east coast; PWA slalom venue and Korea's main scene.

places.name: Omaezaki
places.why: Japan's windsurf capital on a wind-swept cape; PWA slalom venue with spring westerlies.

places.name: Kanaha Beach (Kite Beach)
places.why: Trade winds across the North Shore reef; the sport's spiritual home for both kiting and windsurfing.

places.name: Ho'okipa
places.why: The world's most photographed windsurf wave; Aloha Classic contests every autumn.

places.name: Kailua Beach
places.why: Trade-wind bay on windward Oahu where kiteboarding was pioneered; turquoise water and reef.

places.name: Safety Bay (The Pond)
places.why: Flat-water lagoon behind a sandbar in Perth's southern suburbs; the Fremantle Doctor daily in summer.

places.name: Leighton Beach
places.why: Fremantle's windsurf and kite beach where the summer sea breeze hits first and hardest.

places.name: Lancelin
places.why: Reef-protected bay and Ocean Classic downwinder from Ledge Point; summer sea breezes and dunes.

places.name: Coronation Beach
places.why: Consistent 25-knot summer south-westerlies and a side-shore wave; a windsurf pilgrimage.

places.name: Gnaraloo
places.why: Remote station coast with long reef waves and strong southerlies; 4WD and camping only.

places.name: Brighton Beach, Melbourne
places.why: Port Phillip Bay kite beach by the bathing boxes; south-westerly sea breezes and chop.

places.name: Kyeemagh, Botany Bay
places.why: Sydney's flat-water kite bay next to the airport runway; the nor'easter sea breeze in summer.

places.name: Lyall Bay
places.why: Wellington's south-coast beach with the city's famous northerlies and southerlies and Cook Strait swell.

places.name: Anse Vata
places.why: Lagoon-front beach in the capital with south-east trades; PWA slalom raced here.

places.name: Muri Lagoon
places.why: Shallow lagoon with four motu and steady trades; Rarotonga's kite school beach.

places.name: Hood River Event Site
places.why: Columbia Gorge thermals blow against the river current; the birthplace of American windsurfing.

places.name: The Hatchery
places.why: Spring Creek Hatchery, the Gorge's classic swell spot; nuking westerlies and river waves.

places.name: Crissy Field
places.why: Sail under the Golden Gate in strong summer westerlies and big ebb tides; experts only.

places.name: Sherman Island
places.why: Delta levee spot where the sea breeze funnels inland; warm flat water and reliable afternoon wind.

places.name: Waddell Creek
places.why: Highway 1 wave spot with north-westerlies and Pacific swell; a California windsurf classic.

places.name: Pistol River
places.why: Site of the Pistol River Wave Bash; summer north wind and cold Pacific waves.

places.name: Floras Lake
places.why: Lake separated from the ocean by a dune; warm flat water with the same coast wind.

places.name: Canadian Hole
places.why: Pamlico Sound flat water at Kite Point and Atlantic waves across the road; the East Coast hub.

places.name: Bird Island Basin
places.why: Laguna Madre's shallow flats inside Padre Island National Seashore; wind most days of the year.

places.name: South Padre Island
places.why: Bay side flats and Gulf surf on one barrier island; steady south-easterlies.

places.name: Crandon Park, Key Biscayne
places.why: Miami's kite beach with winter cold fronts and easterly trades over shallow flats.

places.name: Kalmus Beach
places.why: Nantucket Sound's south-westerly sea breeze arrives most summer afternoons; sandy and sheltered.

places.name: Squamish Spit
places.why: Thermal inflow up Howe Sound between granite walls; windy nearly every summer afternoon.

places.name: Nitinat Lake
places.why: Long fjord lake where the thermal blows daily; camp-and-sail with no cell coverage.

places.name: Îles-de-la-Madeleine
places.why: Gulf of St Lawrence archipelago of dunes and lagoons; Canada's most consistent wind.

places.name: La Ventana
places.why: El Norte blows down the Sea of Cortez all winter; campground launch and warm chop.

places.name: Los Barriles
places.why: Baja's original windsurf town with the same winter northerlies and a sandy launch.

places.name: Progreso
places.why: Gulf of Mexico flats with winter Nortes and spring sea breezes; Mérida's beach.

places.name: El Cuyo
places.why: Sleepy fishing village with a long shallow beach and reliable winter-spring wind.

places.name: Isla Blanca
places.why: Sand spit north of Cancún with a knee-deep lagoon; trade winds most of the year.

places.name: Placencia
places.why: Peninsula tip with easterly trades and reef-sheltered water.

places.name: Bahía Salinas
places.why: Papagayo winds funnel across Costa Rica's northwest bay; 30-knot days from December.

places.name: Punta Chame
places.why: Tip of a long sand peninsula on the Pacific side; dry-season trades and huge low-tide flats.

places.name: Cayo Guillermo
places.why: Shallow flats on Cuba's northern cays with winter trades.

places.name: Barkers Beach
places.why: North Sound flats where the easterly trades are cleanest; the island's kite beach.

places.name: Kite Beach, Cabarete
places.why: Trade wind builds each afternoon; flat inside the reef, waves outside, and a whole town built on kiting.

places.name: Buen Hombre
places.why: Fishing village on the north-west coast with a reef lagoon; stronger, drier trades than Cabarete.

places.name: Isla Verde Kite Beach
places.why: Trade-wind city beach beside the airport; easy launch and chop.

places.name: Long Bay Beach
places.why: Waist-deep turquoise flats for miles; trade winds and beginner-perfect water.

places.name: Jabberwock Beach
places.why: Antigua's kite beach on the north-east coast; side-onshore trades and a shallow bay.

places.name: Silver Sands
places.why: South-coast trade-wind spot with a reef wave; a windsurf classic since the 1980s.

places.name: Cas en Bas
places.why: Reef-sheltered bay on the north-east tip with trades and a kite centre.

places.name: Union Island
places.why: Reef flats off Clifton with steady trades; small island, big kite reputation.

places.name: Fisherman's Huts (Hadicurari)
places.why: Aruba's kite and windsurf beach with trade winds 300 days a year and warm flat water.

places.name: Atlantis Beach
places.why: Bonaire's kite beach on the south-west tip; constant trades and clear reef water.

places.name: El Yaque
places.why: Trade winds and standing-depth water made El Yaque a windsurf and kite destination.

places.name: Los Roques
places.why: Coral archipelago with mirror-flat lagoons and trade winds; boat-accessed kiting.

places.name: Adícora
places.why: Paraguaná peninsula town where the trade wind blows nearly every day; Venezuela's kite school.

places.name: Cabo de la Vela
places.why: Desert peninsula with Wayuu villages and 25-knot trades across a flat bay.

places.name: Salinas del Rey
places.why: GKA Kite World Tour venue between Cartagena and Barranquilla; strong trades and a beach wave.

places.name: Santa Marianita
places.why: Ecuador's kite beach with a long side-onshore season and Pacific chop.

places.name: Paracas
places.why: The Paracas wind blows over a desert bay; flat water beside the national reserve.

places.name: Máncora
places.why: Northern Peru's surf town where afternoon southerlies suit wave kiting.

places.name: Matanzas
places.why: Chile's windsurf and kite village with strong summer southerlies and long lefts.

places.name: Cuesta del Viento
places.why: Reservoir in the Andean foothills with a thermal that blows 25 knots every afternoon.

places.name: Laguna Garzón
places.why: Coastal lagoon east of Punta del Este; flat water and summer sea breezes.

places.name: Lagoa da Conceição
places.why: Big lagoon in the middle of the island with steady north-easterlies; Brazil's southern kite hub.

places.name: Ibiraquera
places.why: Shallow lagoon next to Praia do Rosa; light-wind foiling and beginner water.

places.name: Cumbuco
places.why: Brazil's kite gateway: trade winds from July to January, dune lagoons behind and chop in front.

places.name: Lagoa do Cauípe
places.why: Freshwater lagoon behind the dunes near Cumbuco; the flat-water freestyle training ground.

places.name: Taíba
places.why: Small village with a sea spot and a lagoon; trade winds and a beach wave.

places.name: Ilha do Guajiru
places.why: Huge tidal flat that fills into a mirror lagoon; a flat-water freestyle destination.

places.name: Preá
places.why: Long beach 12 km east of Jeri with side-shore trades; base for Jericoacoara riders.

places.name: Jericoacoara
places.why: Dune village on a headland with side-shore trades and wave spots; GKA freestyle has run here.

places.name: Barra Grande
places.why: Flat, shallow bay in Piauí's short coastline; a rising trade-wind kite town.

places.name: Atins
places.why: Rio Preguiças mouth beside the Lençóis dunes; flat river water and a long downwinder finish.

places.name: São Miguel do Gostoso
places.why: Corner of Brazil's north-east where the trade blows side-shore; several schools, few crowds.

places.name: Galinhos
places.why: Peninsula village reached by boat with a flat estuary channel and strong trades.

places.name: Praia do Farol, Icaraí de Amontada
places.why: Icaraizinho's downwinder beach with side-shore trade and a river flat; quieter than Cumbuco.

places.name: Ninh Chu Bay
places.why: Crescent bay east of Phan Rang with a steady dry-season monsoon and flat inner water; hosted the Kiteboard Tour Asia.

places.name: Mandvi Beach
places.why: Wide Arabian Sea beach below a 16th-century fort; India's main kite scene rides the summer monsoon flow.

places.name: Thulusdhoo
places.why: Reef-pass island near Malé with a sandbank for kiting beside the Cokes surf break; windiest in the dry monsoon.

places.name: L'Étang-Salé
places.why: Black-sand reef point on Réunion's south-west coast; the trade-wind swell makes it the island's top wave spot.

places.name: Workum (It Soal)
places.why: IJsselmeer beach with a long, shallow entry before the chop starts; a mainstay of Dutch flat-water kiting.

places.name: Blagoveshenskaya
places.why: Russia's best-known kite spit on the Black Sea; a narrow strip of land lets riders choose the flat side or the chop.

places.name: Bozcaada (Çayır Bay)
places.why: North Aegean island where Çayır Bay gets the strongest Meltemi and Ayazma Beach the calmer, beginner-friendly wind.

places.name: Ain Sokhna
places.why: Red Sea town two hours from Cairo with steady onshore wind nearly every day; several kite centres line the beach.

places.name: Yzerfontein
places.why: West Coast harbour town where the summer south-easter builds a clean, powerful wave for advanced riders.

places.name: Villa Gesell
places.why: Wide dune-backed Atlantic beach with a reliable summer thermal from the north-east most afternoons.

places.name: Sandbanks Provincial Park
places.why: Warm, shallow bay side of a dune park on Lake Ontario; the region's easiest lake-kiting water.

places.name: Vama Veche
places.why: Romania's southernmost beach town on the Black Sea; a steady northerly makes it the country's kite hub.

places.name: Kanali
places.why: Ionian bay behind a spit where a valley thermal builds through the afternoon; a GKA freestyle stop.

places.name: Nabq Bay
places.why: Shallow Red Sea bay north of Sharm El Sheikh with a Bedouin-run kite centre and a near-constant thermal.

places.name: Kuta, Lombok
places.why: South-coast bay with a shallow lagoon inside the reef and bigger swell outside; dry-season trades peak mid-year.

places.name: Le Touquet
places.why: Wide Channel beach at the Canche estuary; a historic French wind-sports resort since the 1920s.

places.name: Che Shale
places.why: Secluded 5 km beach north of Malindi ranked among East Africa's top kite spots; both the Kaskazi and Kusi trades deliver.

places.name: Geribá, Búzios
places.why: Búzios' longest beach faces the open Atlantic; strong summer trades and rough water suit experienced riders.

places.name: Nananu-i-Ra
places.why: Small island off Viti Levu's north coast where wind funnels between Fiji's two main islands; the country's kite and windsurf base.
